```Dockerfile
# Use the official Go 1.22 base image
FROM golang:1.22

# Set the working directory in the container
WORKDIR /go/src/app

# Copy the current directory contents into the container at /go/src/app
COPY . .

# Build the Go application
RUN go build -o server .

# Expose port 8080 for the server to listen on
EXPOSE 8080

# Define environment variable(s)
ENV NAME World

# Make port 8080 available to the world outside this container
CMD ["./server"]
```

### Explanation:

1. **Base Image**: The `FROM golang:1.22` line specifies that the Docker image will be based on the official Golang 1.22 image.

2. **Working Directory**: The `WORKDIR /go/src/app` line sets the working directory inside the container where all the source code will be placed.

3. **Copy Files**: The `COPY . .` line copies the entire contents of the current directory (the directory containing the Dockerfile) into the `/go/src/app` directory in the container.

4. **Build Application**: The `RUN go build -o server .` line compiles the Go program located in the `/go/src/app` directory and places the resulting binary file named `server` in the same directory.

5. **Expose Port**: The `EXPOSE 8080` line makes the port 8080 available to the world outside the container, allowing it to be accessed from other machines.

6. **Define Environment Variable**: The `ENV NAME World` line defines an environment variable named `NAME` with a default value of "World".

7. **Start Command**: The `CMD ["./server"]` line specifies the command to run when the container starts. In this case, it runs the `server` binary.

This Dockerfile provides a complete setup for building and running a simple Go web server within a Docker container.
